title: SYSK Selects: How Circumcision Works
summary: A rerun Selects episode of Stuff You Should Know, originally published November 2014 (per the hosts' on-air framing), on how circumcision works. Covers a proposed San Francisco ballot measure by Lloyd Scofield to criminalize circumcision of minors; US circumcision rates falling; the anatomy of the foreskin (prepuce), frenulum and glans; medical problems like phimosis, paraphimosis and balanitis; religious and historical origins from Genesis/Abraham, ancient Egypt, Colchians, Mayans and Aztecs, and 19th-century Western medicine; global practice including Africa, South Korea and the Philippines; the procedure and devices (Gomco clamp, Plastibell); arguments for and against circumcision including HPV and HIV claims, AAP stance, and risks; restoration methods (epipasm); female genital mutilation; and listener mail about finger amputations.

segments.title: Intro and San Francisco circumcision ballot proposal
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the episode and discuss Lloyd Scofield's proposed San Francisco ballot measure to make circumcising anyone under eighteen a misdemeanor, and the debate over parental choice.

segments.title: Circumcision rates in the United States
segments.summary: Statistics on US circumcision rates falling over three decades, regional differences, the role of the Hispanic population, and the cost of the procedure.

segments.title: Anatomy of the foreskin
segments.summary: Definition of circumcision, the prepuce (foreskin), glans, and frenulum, and the foreskin's protective and sensitive functions.

segments.title: Medical problems related to the foreskin
segments.summary: Hygiene and smegma, phimosis (too tight), paraphimosis (too loose), balanoposthitis, and tight frenulum; the hosts note these problems are rare and circumcision is rarely medically necessary.

segments.title: Origins and religious history of circumcision
segments.summary: Biblical origins in the covenant with Abraham, Judaism and Islam traditions, Egyptian origins, and other ancient and indigenous groups practicing circumcision, including the Colchians, Mayans and Aztecs.

segments.title: Western medicine and circumcision in the 19th century
segments.summary: How circumcision became associated with Western medicine in the nineteenth century, with claims it could treat masturbation-related conditions, and the role of barbers and mohels.

segments.title: Circumcision practices around the world
segments.summary: Age of circumcision across cultures, rites of passage, risks in areas without trained practitioners in Africa, and prevalence in South Korea and the Philippines linked to American servicemen.

segments.title: The circumcision procedure and devices
segments.summary: Description of infant circumcision with restraint and anesthesia, the Gomco clamp and Plastibell device, recovery time, and adult circumcision technique.

segments.title: Arguments for and against circumcision
segments.summary: Reasons parents choose circumcision (religion, culture, social conformity, HPV, syphilis, chlamydia, HIV studies) and arguments against it (mutilation, unnecessary procedure per AAP, complications, loss of sensitivity, right to choose, foreskin restoration methods).

segments.title: Female genital mutilation comparison
segments.summary: Discussion of female genital mutilation and its historical Western parallel, including clitoridectomy in the United States, and the WHO and UN response.

segments.title: Listener mail on finger amputations and sign-off
segments.summary: Listener stories about missing fingers, including a woodworking injury, polydactyly, and a factory accident, followed by a sign-off.
